questions.q: What is the main scope difference between a data warehouse and a data mart?
options: A warehouse covers the whole organization; a mart is narrowed to one business function
A mart is always larger than a warehouse
A warehouse can only hold unstructured data; a mart only holds structured data
There is no difference in scope between the two
questions.explain: A mart is a scaled-down, department-focused slice of the same underlying subject matter.

questions.q: What is the schema-timing difference between a data lake and a data warehouse?
options: A lake applies schema on read; a warehouse applies schema on write
Both apply schema at exactly the same time
A warehouse never uses any schema at all
A lake requires schema to be defined twice
questions.explain: This is the core distinction from Lesson 110 — lakes defer structure to query time, warehouses lock it in before loading.

questions.q: In a mature BI pipeline, how do a lake, a warehouse, and a mart typically relate to each other?
options: Raw data lands in the lake first, a curated subset moves into the warehouse, and individual teams get their own mart carved from the warehouse
They are three interchangeable names for the exact same technology
A warehouse must be deleted before a lake can be created
A mart always contains more data than the warehouse it comes from
questions.explain: They typically form a pipeline rather than compete as alternatives for the same job.

options: A hybrid combining a lake's cheap, flexible storage with a warehouse's structured query layer, without physically copying data twice
A physical building where data lake servers are stored
A deprecated term with no modern equivalent
A synonym for a data mart
questions.explain: Platforms like Azure Synapse and Delta Lake implement this hybrid pattern in production.

questions.q: In AdventureWorksDW2014, what would querying just FactResellerSales and its dimensions represent, versus querying the whole FactInternetSales-and-FactResellerSales set?
options: The mart-level slice versus the full warehouse-level view
The lake-level view versus the mart-level view
Two completely unrelated databases with no comparison possible
The OLTP source versus the OLAP destination
questions.explain: Narrowing to one fact table and its dimensions is exactly the mart pattern from Lesson 109, applied within the same warehouse.
